ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a schematic diagram of the Harbin-Dalian High-Speed Railway; the line generally runs in a southwest-northeast direction, connecting important northeastern cities such as Dalian, Shenyang, Changchun, and Harbin, and beside it there is an illustration of a high-speed train. Then reason: the question stem asks about the “decisive factor in high-speed railway construction.” High-speed railway construction requires enormous investment; whether it can be built mainly depends on the economic development level of cities along the line, population and passenger flow demand, regional connections, and social development needs. Natural conditions such as severe cold will increase construction difficulty, but with progress in engineering technology, they usually are limiting factors rather than decisive factors. Therefore, the decisive factor in high-speed railway construction is socioeconomic.
